events.summary: iOS 5.0.1 Beta 1 is represented by 6 editorially reviewed, source-backed records from the 2011-11-02 milestone; unsupported routes and builds are excluded, while cumulative context is labeled explicitly.

blocks.text: Opening the maintenance cycle

Contemporaneous release coverage places the first 5.0.1 developer seed on November 2, 2011. The surviving Apple Developer entry displays November 3, so this page keeps the release-day identity and records the one-day source mismatch.

citations.locator: Release date — Wednesday November 2, 2011 2:38 pm PDT
Apple page date — November 3, 2011

blocks.text: Selected milestone records

Six source-linked records describe the seed's maintenance scope: four broad reliability or usability items, one security repair identified in a contemporary recap, and one first-party storage-management API.

blocks.text: Second developer seed
A release-day report identifies the second iOS 5.0.1 beta on November 4, two days after the opening seed.

citations.locator: Release date — Friday November 4, 2011 10:49 am PDT

blocks.text: Narrow evidence boundary

No public changelog was available at the time. One contemporaneous account connected Beta 2 to activation failures in the prior build and reported no broader visible delta, so only that repair is structured here.

blocks.text: End of the beta interval
The first-party Public notice followed on November 10. This archive batch adds no intermediate route and makes no build-number claim.

events.summary: iOS 5.1 Beta 1 is represented by 12 editorially reviewed, source-backed records from the 2011-11-28 milestone; unsupported routes and builds are excluded, while cumulative context is labeled explicitly.

blocks.text: First iOS 5.1 developer seed
Contemporaneous reporting identifies the first 5.1 beta on November 28, 2011. A preserved three-page Apple-authored PDF provides the detailed milestone state.

citations.locator: Release date — Monday November 28, 2011 3:45 pm PST
Artifact title — iOS SDK Release Notes for iOS 5.1 beta 1

blocks.text: Selected developer-note state

Twelve records capture API behavior, current limitations, and one explicit Newsstand repair. Ten unmarked or explicitly older states are labeled cumulative context; the peer-to-peer default and marked Newsstand repair remain milestone deltas. Three cumulative records concern the accompanying Xcode and developer-tools environment, so they are retained as host-tool context rather than on-device iOS behavior. This is a selected view rather than a transcription of the full document.

changes.title: Peer-to-peer service-discovery defaults
changes.canonicalSummary: DNS service-discovery calls stopped including peer-to-peer interfaces unless an application requested them explicitly.
changes.summary: Service-discovery APIs required explicit peer-to-peer inclusion instead of searching those interfaces automatically.
changes.verificationMethod: The byte-verified Apple-authored PDF states the revised default and names the affected API families.

citations.locator: Networking — NSNetService class and CFNetService APIs do not include P2P interfaces by default

changes.title: Game Center profile-media loading
changes.canonicalSummary: Game Center integrations could fail to display application icons and user profile images.
changes.summary: Applications using Game Center could show neither their icons nor players' profile images.
changes.verificationMethod: The preserved Apple-authored notes list the rendering failure as current Beta 1 state.

citations.locator: Game Center — App Icons and Profile Photos are not loading in apps using Game Center

changes.title: iCloud provisioning-profile enablement
changes.canonicalSummary: Provisioning profiles needed explicit iCloud enablement before an application could use cloud storage.
changes.summary: Using iCloud storage depended on a provisioning profile that had been enabled for the service.
changes.verificationMethod: The retained Apple-authored document states the provisioning prerequisite.

citations.locator: iCloud Storage — Provisioning profiles must be enabled for iCloud

changes.title: NSMetadataQuery sorting
changes.canonicalSummary: The prerelease iCloud document implementation did not support NSMetadataQuery sort descriptors.
changes.summary: The first 5.1 seed continued to lack sort-descriptor support in metadata queries.

citations.locator: iCloud Storage — setSortDescriptors: method of NSMetadataQuery is not supported

changes.title: Protected-data cloud documents
changes.canonicalSummary: Combining cloud-document APIs with protected data could corrupt stored content.
changes.summary: Cloud-document storage remained incompatible with files guarded by Data Protection.
changes.verificationMethod: The Apple-authored PDF directly records the incompatibility for this milestone.

citations.locator: iCloud Storage — files that are protected via Data Protection cannot be used with iCloud Storage APIs

changes.title: iCloud filename case handling
changes.canonicalSummary: iCloud Storage treated file names as case-sensitive.
changes.summary: Different filename case rules across Mac and iOS still created a cloud-document interoperability risk.
changes.verificationMethod: The preserved developer notes contrast the two platforms' filename behavior.

citations.locator: iCloud Storage — File names are case-insensitive in Mac OS X but case-sensitive in iOS

changes.summary: Applications needed to prepare a newly created movie player before starting playback.

events.summary: iOS 5.1 Beta 3 is represented by 2 editorially reviewed, source-backed records from the 2012-01-09 milestone; unsupported routes and builds are excluded, while cumulative context is labeled explicitly.

blocks.text: Third iOS 5.1 developer seed
Beta 3 appeared on January 9, 2012. The structured delta is limited to a documented backup-exclusion API and a separately reported return of the 3G control.

citations.locator: Release date — Monday January 9, 2012 10:38 am PST
Release-note API — add the NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey attribute to prevent the corresponding file from being backed up
Observed setting — new build restores the toggle that allows users to turn off 3G cellular data access

blocks.text: Why the route sequence stops here

Apple still directed 5.1 developers to beta tooling on February 16. March reporting described partner testing of an internal Gold Master, while a post-release walkthrough says Apple did not provide developers a final test build before the March 7 Public release. Those facts do not establish a developer GM route.

citations.locator: February developer state — continue to use Xcode 4.3 Developer Preview with iOS 5.1 SDK beta
Internal distribution — three different partners who are testing the Gold Master
Developer GM boundary — Apple didn't release any final build for developers to test against
Public date — March 7, 2012

blocks.text: No inferred 5.1.1 beta
Apple's consumer archive separately lists 5.1 and 5.1.1, but it does not identify a prerelease seed. Because no exact 5.1.1 beta identity was recovered, this batch creates none.
